title: Deterministic Preparation of Arbitrary Spin Eigenfunctions
authors: Wenxuan Tao, Jianan Wang, Fen Zuo
abstract: Quantum states with conserved total spins, or spin eigenfunctions, are important for studying quantum chemistry and quantum manybody physics problems. A typical class of spin eigenfunctions are Dicke states, which attain maximal spins. While we already have many efficient quantum algorithms to prepare Dicke states, it is not yet clear if we could do so for arbitrary spin eigenfunctions deterministically. Generalizing Bärtschi and Eidenbenz's elegant algorithms for Dicke state preparation, we successfully prepare arbitrary spin eigenfunctions characterized by branching paths and binary spin trees. As a byproduct, we also develop the corresponding classical algorithms to reconstruct all these spin states.
summary: This work develops a general quantum circuit protocol to deterministically prepare any arbitrary spin eigenstate, extending previous methods designed for simpler Dicke states. By mapping the state structure onto a branching diagram, the authors derive recursive unitary operators based on coupling coefficients. This provides a powerful tool for simulating complex quantum many-body systems relevant to condensed matter physics.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of deterministically preparing arbitrary spin eigenfunctions, generalizing known efficient preparation methods for simpler states like Dicke states.
main_result: The authors successfully generalize the preparation techniques using a branching diagram approach, constructing the required unitary operators as products of sequential coupling gates.
method: The methodology involves translating techniques from established state preparation algorithms (like WDB and SCS) into a general framework characterized by branching paths and binary spin trees.
model_or_system: The system involves coupled spin-1/2 particles whose total spin eigenfunctions are the focus. The states are characterized by total spin quantum numbers and branching path symbols.
key_observables: Spin state amplitudes, total spin quantum numbers (S, Sz), and the structure of the branching diagram.
important_parameters: The number of spins ($n$), the target total spin ($S$), and the specific coupling coefficients derived from Clebsch-Gordan theory.
main_assumptions: The construction relies on recursive relations derived from Clebsch-Gordan coefficients and assumes the implementability of the derived controlled rotation gates.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the circuit diagrams for the WDB and SCS modules, the branching diagram structure for small $n$, and the specific duplication and elimination modules used in the circuit construction.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from reviewing Dicke state preparation (SCS/WDB) to introducing the general framework using branching diagrams. It then derives recursive circuit construction formulas and details the implementation of complex modules like the negative-logic WDB circuit.
why_interesting: The ability to deterministically prepare complex, highly entangled spin states is foundational for simulating quantum many-body physics, which is central to strongly correlated electron systems.
